clauses.reason: The order exempts Samuel A. Cottrell from compulsory retirement for age and fixes its own end in the sentence "hereby exempt the said Samuel A. Cottrell from compulsory retirement for age for a period of one year ending September 30, 1940". The exemption therefore ran through September 30, 1940, and that date is recorded as the first end, inclusive; the exclusive reading (the exemption ends as September 30, 1940 begins) is the alternative, and it would put the end one day earlier. The ending is the order's own stated term and the acting instrument is EO 8262 itself. The only operative sentence is the quoted one; the recital states the finding that the public interest requires the exemption and commands nothing else. Later events recorded for this clause: EO 8555 of September 28, 1940 states "I hereby further exempt the said Samuel A. Cottrell from compulsory retirement for age for a period of nine months ending June 30, 1941"; it cites this order by number, grants a further exemption for a later period, and is recorded as a later event; it does not alter the period stated in this order. EO 8805 of June 25, 1941 states "I hereby further exempt the said Samuel A. Cottrell from compulsory retirement for age for a period of one year ending June 30, 1942"; it cites this order by number, grants a further exemption for a later period, and is recorded as a later event; it does not alter the period stated in this order. Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 each further exemption is a later event with its own date and quotation and is not this order's end.

research_rationale:
EO 8262 (1939-09-26, Franklin D. Roosevelt), a one-person exemption from compulsory retirement for age. Text and identity: the held text is the American Presidency Project transcription (grade mirror_transcription, acceptable_as_original false; standing note: original not yet held). Page check per jobs/claim-kit/AGENT_PROTOCOL.md: the APP page record with the same sha256 in jobs/app-executive-orders/output/MIRROR_DOCUMENTS.jsonl (common-crawl capture) has the heading "Executive Order 8262—Exemption of Samuel A. Cottrell From Compulsory Retirement for Age", which names this order number, its date (1939-09-26) agrees with the held text, and its text_sha256 equals the held file's. I read the whole text: one recital and one operative sentence, so the clause inventory is the single whole-paragraph clause. The sentence "hereby exempt the said Samuel A. Cottrell from compulsory retirement for age for a period of one year ending September 30, 1940" fixes the end of the exemption on September 30, 1940; that is the first end, with the exclusive reading disclosed. The packet's later-events search (Federal Register disposition notes of 6938 catalog records from 1937 onward, plus operative sentences in 17521 saved order texts) returned two hits, "See" cross-references to the later further-exemption orders EO 8555 and EO 8805. The packet's name search of held order texts for the person named in this order is also cited. Other leads and later events are discussed in the clause reason. No held source shows an earlier end (revocation, supersession, or an earlier separation or death of the employee), so none is claimed.
